title: FREYA Rev09 — requirement evidence assessment
baseline: Revision 5.1, source FDS-001 Rev09; A/B default inputs, not current slider trades
meaning: Simulation supported means a successful numerical subcheck under stated assumptions. Partial means only part of the requirement is addressed. Flight heritage means an analogous demonstrated element, not FREYA qualification. No requirement is marked fully verified.

H-PATH.citation: NASA Planetary Data System. Mars Pathfinder Lander Description. ASI/MET EDL archive, instrument-host documentation, undated. Sections: Entry, Descent, and Landing; Attitude and Information Management; Power and Pyrotechnics.
H-PATH.demonstrated: Pathfinder demonstrated a blunt-cone SLA-561V entry system, parachute descent, staged separations, onboard timing and radar-triggered events. It also used Sun sensing and integrated command/data handling. This is function-level heritage at different mass, geometry and flight conditions.

H-MEDLI.citation: NASA. Sensors Collect Crucial Data on Mars Landings with Arrival of Perseverance. 1 April 2021.
H-MEDLI.demonstrated: Perseverance landed successfully on 18 February 2021. MEDLI2 returned heat-shield/back-shell heating and pressure measurements, including stored entry data after landing. This supports the existence of measured entry environments, not calibration of FREYA’s thermal model.

H-MARCO.citation: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory. InSight Landing Press Kit: Mars Cube One. 2018. Achievements to date and technology suppliers.
H-MARCO.demonstrated: MarCO completed in-space trajectory corrections and propulsion/radio demonstrations using spacecraft equipped with cold-gas propulsion. This does not demonstrate FREYA’s nitrogen tank, six-jet geometry, orbital deorbit motor or feed system.

H-KEPLER.citation: NASA Science. Kepler / K2. Mission history, undated webpage.
H-KEPLER.demonstrated: Kepler used four reaction wheels for precision pointing. Wheel failures later forced a different operating approach; heritage therefore includes a reliability caution, not a guarantee of FREYA controllability.

H-NAV.citation: NASA Science. Surviving an In-Flight Anomaly: What Happened on Ingenuity’s Sixth Flight. 27 May 2021.
H-NAV.demonstrated: Ingenuity flew with camera/IMU navigation and landed safely after an image-timing anomaly on Flight Six. This is visual-inertial navigation heritage in low-altitude flight, not orbital limb navigation or FREYA covariance verification.

H-COMPUTE.citation: Cretu, V.; Ogut, M.; Swope, J.; Dunkel, E.; Mirza, F.; Chien, S.; Jongeling, A.; Sheldon, D.; Sauvageau, J.; Ogbe, D.; Towfic, Z. J. Benchmarking and Testing of Qualcomm Snapdragon System-on-Chip for JPL Space Applications and Missions. JPL, 5 March 2022. NTRS 20230006988.
H-COMPUTE.demonstrated: JPL reports Snapdragon 801 use aboard Ingenuity on Mars. It is evidence for a flown commercial processor in a different architecture, not flight proof of Raspberry Pi hardware, ML limb detection, or FREYA safety partitioning.

H-RELAY.citation: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory. The Mars Relay Network Connects Us to NASA’s Martian Explorers. 16 February 2021.
H-RELAY.demonstrated: Mars surface missions have used orbiter relay paths to return science and engineering data to Earth. Existing network operation does not establish FREYA link access, waveform compatibility, coverage or a 95% retention guarantee.

H-VIKING.citation: NASA Science. Viking Spacecraft and Science. Mission retrospective, undated webpage.
H-VIKING.demonstrated: Viking landers separated from Mars-orbiting spacecraft, landed, acquired/analyzed soil and returned surface science. Biology results provided no clear evidence of living microorganisms. This is not proof of FREYA penetrator sampling or life-detection performance.

H-LR.citation: NASA Planetary Data System. Viking Lander 1 Spacecraft Labeled Release. Instrument context urn:nasa:pds:context:instrument:lr1.vl1, undated.
H-LR.demonstrated: The flown Viking LR instrument measured labeled-gas release and included heat-sterilized controls. Its aqueous nutrient method and detectors differ from FREYA’s proposed protocols; flight heritage does not prove those protocols or a biological interpretation.

H-PP.citation: NASA. NASA Planetary Protection Handbook, Version 1.0. NASA/SP-20240016475. December 2024. Historical Viking sterilization and bioburden verification discussion.
H-PP.demonstrated: The handbook documents Viking hardware sterilization and biological-cleanliness verification. It supports contamination-control heritage, not the applicable classification, accepted plan or verified cleanliness of FREYA hardware.

H-DS2.citation: NASA Science. Mars Polar Lander / Deep Space 2. Mission retrospective, undated webpage.
H-DS2.demonstrated: Deep Space 2’s two penetrators were lost on arrival in December 1999. Their intended penetration/sampling/telemetry objectives are not successful flight evidence. No failure mechanism or penetration depth is inferred here.

S-DELIVERY-A.title: A nominal per-vehicle delivery
S-DELIVERY-A.criterion: Expected probe count; every propagated probe and carrier reaches h=0.
S-DELIVERY-A.limits: Ground arrival in a point-mass model is not impact survival or successful science. B runs one vehicle; the second identical vehicle is not a coupled simulation.

S-DELIVERY-B.title: B nominal per-vehicle delivery
S-DELIVERY-B.criterion: Expected probe count; every propagated probe and carrier reaches h=0.
S-DELIVERY-B.limits: Ground arrival in a point-mass model is not impact survival or successful science. B runs one vehicle; the second identical vehicle is not a coupled simulation.

S-ORBIT.title: 300 km orbit to descending 125 km interface
S-ORBIT.criterion: Both cases start at 300 km and reach the descending entry interface.
S-ORBIT.limits: Reduced-order deterministic trajectory; no navigation estimation or corridor qualification.

S-GAS.title: Paired-jet momentum, slew and storage closure
S-GAS.criterion: Δv_sep=0.2 m/s; scalar 90° retroburn and 180° heat-shield rest-to-rest slew identities; all three gas withdrawals close; positive gas above minimum pressure.
S-GAS.limits: Ideal N2 at 293 K; assumed inertia; no 3-axis control, hardware feed losses, regulator sizing or fault simulation.

S-ENGINE.title: Nominal finite-burn A/B performance
S-ENGINE.criterion: A nominal Δv ≥ vacuum demand; B nominal Δv closes within 10⁻⁶ m/s.
S-ENGINE.limits: B thrust is sized from the same assumed Isp demand relation, an algebraic closure rather than independent hardware proof. Neither case proves pointing or delivered motor curve.

S-A-MARGIN.title: A reference motor versus 25% planning allowance
S-A-MARGIN.criterion: Achieved A Δv ≥ nominal vacuum demand × 1.25.
S-A-MARGIN.limits: This check intentionally reports the current baseline shortfall; reaching the atmosphere is not margin compliance.

S-TARGET.title: Nominal target screening within source planning radii
S-TARGET.criterion: Nominal closest miss within A 100 km / B 50 km; opportunity in 3–20 orbits.
S-TARGET.limits: Not a 95% Monte Carlo result. Initial geometry/target assumed; no terrain exclusion.

S-ENTRY.title: Finite entry load trajectory
S-ENTRY.criterion: Finite nominal state history reaches assumed 10 km extraction gate.
S-ENTRY.limits: Zero lift and heat-shield-forward attitude are imposed. No attitude stability, structural strength or safe Mach/q deployment limit is tested.

S-THERMAL.title: Finite two-location temperature history
S-THERMAL.criterion: Finite history; center peak exceeds shoulder peak under chosen flow multiplier.
S-THERMAL.limits: Numerical sanity only. Assumed nonablating properties; not material qualification or acceptable shell/electronics temperatures.

S-DESCENT.title: Independent carrier and probe time histories
S-DESCENT.criterion: Finite time-ordered probe trajectories and positive descent duration; default canopy inputs.
S-DESCENT.limits: Linear inflation proxy and scalar drag, not real deployment opening loads or pendulum/attitude stability.

S-RELEASE.title: Altitude gate, cadence and inherited release state
S-RELEASE.criterion: Sequential release, inherited altitude and released probe mass closure.
S-RELEASE.limits: Point bodies do not test mechanical interference, separation clearances or actuator reliability.

S-ATMOSPHERE.title: Density / wind sensitivity
S-ATMOSPHERE.criterion: A changed atmosphere/wind case reaches extraction and changes impact speed.
S-ATMOSPHERE.limits: One combined sensitivity case, not separate attribution, site elevation modeling or a probabilistic atmosphere ensemble.

S-LINK.title: Assumed RF link and duty-cycle screen
S-LINK.criterion: Free-space link margin > 0 dB at the default assumed geometry/receiver.
S-LINK.limits: Not an actual radio, pulse buffer, relay contract, contact schedule, outage/blackout or data-retention test.

S-POWER.title: Surface energy screening with 20% reserve
S-POWER.criterion: Usable energy − average load × duration ≥ 20% of usable energy.
S-POWER.limits: Assumed already-usable capacity and average load; no environmental derating, heater/peak-current waveform or selected battery.

S-STATUS.title: Cumulative payload identities
S-STATUS.criterion: All bits latch at completion, with stable bit identity in A and B.
S-STATUS.limits: Synthetic review markers; not actual sensors, flight 60 s timer, RF reception, nonvolatile reset recovery or science packets.

S-IMPACT.title: Impact-screen analytical identity
S-IMPACT.criterion: Zero inertial-coefficient limit reproduces constant-force work/energy penetration.
S-IMPACT.limits: Uncalibrated material assumptions, no fracture/crush/instrument shock. Mathematical identity is not soil penetration or survival validation.

S-TRACE.title: Complete source identifier preservation
S-TRACE.criterion: 91 distinct source IDs and matching evidence records.
S-TRACE.limits: Does not establish approved acceptance criteria, named owners or full objective/design/anomaly traceability.

provenance.note: Checks use fresh baseline runs. Review is a fixed baseline assessment; changing website sliders does not alter these evidence marks.
